learning_outcomes.text: To have knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of electrical engineering.
To be aware of the multidisciplinary context of electrical engineering.
To be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve electrical engineering problems using established methods.
To be able to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
To have technical and laboratory competencies.
To be able to combine theory and practice to solve electrical engineering problems.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in an area of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge and use of the principles of electrical circuits and the theory of electrical machines.

syllabus_topics: Electrical variables and their measurement units
Elements of electrical circuits: resistors, coils, capacitors, and sources
Circuit analysis in the frequency domain
Practical sessions on current, voltage and power measurements in DC circuits, AC circuits and three-phase systems
teaching_methods: Individual and collective tutorials for resolving student doubts
Individual student work with proposed exercises
Laboratory practicals for assembling electrical circuits and making measurements on them
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment includes three equally weighted partial exams and practical session performance, which accounts for 10% of the continuous assessment grade. Attendance to practical sessions is mandatory for continuous assessment. For the ordinary call, students who pass continuous assessment do not need to take the final exam; their continuous assessment grade becomes the final grade. Otherwise, the final exam grade applies, consisting of three equally weighted exercises and a final laboratory exam for students who did not complete practices. The extraordinary call consists solely of a final exam with three equally weighted exercises and a final laboratory exam for students who did not complete practices.
